findings.description: Length caps (keyboardText <=4096, button text <=64) use Java String.length(), which counts UTF-16 code units, not Unicode code points or Telegram's own length semantics. A payload of supplementary-plane characters (emoji, e.g. 2048 emoji at 2 UTF-16 units each = 4096 .length() but 2048 visible glyphs) passes the cap while a real Telegram body may compute a different length. This is NOT a vulnerability at this layer (the cap is still a hard bound; no overflow/NPE/injection), and it is fully consistent with the existing codebase convention (MAX_KEYWORD_LENGTH at line 654, MAX_BUTTON_LABEL at line 993, @Size on name all use UTF-16 .length()). Telegram-side rejection on send is a Task 3 concern. Flagged only for awareness; no action required for this task.
findings.recommendation: No change required for Task 1. If exact Telegram-grapheme parity ever becomes a requirement, address it uniformly across all funnel text caps (out of scope here).

findings.description: Button label text is stored VERBATIM (no HTML/Markdown escaping, no sanitization) by design — this is correct for a persistence/validation layer. The text is author-controlled (the funnel owner authoring their own keyboard), not arbitrary subscriber input, so there is no stored-XSS trust-boundary crossing introduced here. When this text later reaches a Telegram wire body (Task 3) it is a JSON string value (Jackson-serialized, so quotes/control chars are escaped by the serializer) and is NOT interpolated into a parse_mode-formatted span unless the author sets keyboardParseMode — and reply-keyboard button labels are plain text in Telegram regardless of parse mode. No injection risk is introduced by this layer. The duplicate check uses HashSet on trimmed strings (no regex, no query construction) — no injection surface. Flagged only to record that the no-escape decision was reviewed and is appropriate; defense for the wire body is Task 3's responsibility.
findings.recommendation: No change for Task 1. Task 3 must serialize button text and keyboardText via the JSON client (not string-concatenate into the request body) so author content cannot break out of the JSON structure — recommend carrying this as a Task 3 review note.

summary: No blocking/major/minor security findings. Input validation is complete and matches tech-spec Decision 6: keyboardText non-blank + hard <=4096, parseMode restricted to null|HTML|MarkdownV2 (requireParseMode), rows 1..10, buttons-per-row 1..4, button text non-blank + <=64, duplicate trimmed texts rejected via HashSet. All hostile-payload paths terminate in a clean 422 funnel_step_invalid, never an NPE/500: null rows list, empty rows, null row element, null buttons list, empty buttons list, and null button element are each explicitly guarded in toKeyboardRows and validateSetKeyboard before any field is dereferenced. CLEAR_KEYBOARD applies symmetric strict rejection of keyboardRows/isPersistent/oneTimeKeyboard (empty non-null list still counts as present). Mass-assignment is defended: both new DTOs carry @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true), so unknown fields are silently ignored (no 400/500). Resource exhaustion is bounded — the outer maxSteps cap fires first (validateSteps line 815) and each SET_KEYBOARD is bounded to <=10x4=40 buttons, so the validation iteration is finite. PII rule is satisfied: every invalidStep(...) message names only field names and numeric limits, never echoing author content (button labels or text values). keyboardText is kept verbatim (not blankToNull) so a whitespace-only text is correctly rejected by isBlank(); keyboardParseMode is routed through blankToNull so blank normalizes to null (plain text) with no validation bypass — garbage parse mode hits requireParseMode -> 422. No hardcoded secrets, no SSRF, no deserialization risk introduced at this layer. AuthZ/CSRF are enforced upstream at the controller (unchanged). Two info-level notes recorded (UTF-16 vs grapheme length counting consistent with existing codebase convention; verbatim button-text storage with escaping deferred to Task 3 wire-body construction) — neither requires action in Task 1. Status: approved.
